solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Woman suffering reverse in July rebellion

indicators.note: suffering reverse says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the letters sit inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A woman has a setback during a summer uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft left 'in' unexplained; it is the signal that the letters lie within 'July rebellion'. LYREB is found there, and 'suffering reverse' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, so any female given name fits the bare definition.

clue.text: Oxbridge competition upset old boy a bit

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so these letters read upwards

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
a trace is a tiny bit or amount

explanation.surface: An Oxbridge contest has slightly upset a former pupil.
explanation.walkthrough: The Boat Race is the annual rowing contest on the Thames between Oxford and Cambridge universities.
explanation.definitionFit: The rowing race between Oxford and Cambridge is the best-known Oxbridge sporting contest.

clue.text: Unyielding US soldier, free to go outside

indicators.note: the word for free is told to go around the outside of the soldier

parts.note: to rid is to free, as in rid of pests
GI is the familiar name for an American soldier

explanation.surface: A stubborn American soldier is told he may leave the base.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: something stiff and unbending is unyielding.

clue.text: Set free, one gets told off after end of trial

indicators.note: after places the following pieces behind the last letter of trial
end of picks out the final letter of the word trial

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one
to be berated is to be told off or scolded

explanation.surface: A prisoner freed at the close of a trial still gets a scolding.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: a person released from captivity has been freed.

clue.text: Frisk medic entering jail

indicators.note: the doctor's letters go into the word for prison

parts.note: gaol is the British spelling of jail
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, stands for a doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor going into a prison is searched by guards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frisk' suggests a body search, but here it means to leap about playfully.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean to skip and caper about playfully, as lambs do.

clue.text: This compiler's pursuing a goal

indicators.note: pursuing means following, so these letters come after the article

parts.note: the setter refers to themself; this compiler is = I am, contracted

explanation.surface: The setter is chasing an objective.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: an objective or target one strives for.

clue.text: During contest the Spanish tenor's beginning to sing loudly

indicators.note: during says the following pieces fall within the word for a contest

parts.note: a bout is a contest, as in boxing
el is Spanish for the

indicators.note: beginning takes just the opening letter of tenor's

explanation.surface: In a competition, a Spanish tenor starts singing at full volume.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to deliver a song with great force and volume.

clue.text: Girl not first in school group

indicators.note: the word for a school group loses its opening letter

parts.note: a class is a group of pupils taught together

explanation.surface: A girl fails to come top in her year.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: a young woman, chiefly in Scottish and northern English use.

clue.text: Surprisingly West Peru's an unexplored area

indicators.note: surprisingly says these letters turn up in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: Western Peru, oddly, is still uncharted territory.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom from Milton: fresh, untried territory or a new field of activity.

clue.text: Lab gear prepared for lesson in school

indicators.note: prepared means made ready, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Laboratory equipment is set up for a school class.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a science class, but the subject is a branch of mathematics.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a mathematics subject taught as a class in schools.

clue.text: Everything is available in M & S shopping centres

indicators.note: the word for everything is placed inside the store's letters

parts.note: the letters M and S taken as written
all means everything

explanation.surface: A boast that Marks & Spencer stocks everything.
explanation.walkthrough: M & S is Marks & Spencer, a well-known British department store chain.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: large covered precincts of shops.

clue.text: Embarrassed-looking left-winger

definitions.meaning: flushed in the face with shame
a socialist or communist, from the colour of the radical flag

explanation.definitionFit: The colour of a blush, and the colour of socialism.

clue.text: Going round helping to carry biblical books

indicators.note: the portion word holds the books inside it

parts.note: a ration is a helping or allotted portion
OT is the Old Testament

explanation.surface: Doing the rounds while helping to lug Bibles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'helping' looks like a verb but is a noun meaning a portion.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: turning around an axis, spinning.

clue.text: Cutting freshwater fish, worker will keep tail for later

indicators.note: the fish holds the extra letter inside it

parts.note: a tench is a European freshwater fish

indicators.note: tail takes the final letter of later

parts.note: the worker ant is the crossword's usual worker

explanation.surface: A fish and a worker are cut while saving a tail for another time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tail for later' reads as an instruction to postpone, but it is the last letter of 'later'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: a trenchant remark is incisive or sharply cutting.

clue.text: Victorian killer in extremely flashy showy attire

indicators.note: in places the killer inside the outer letters
extremely takes the two extreme letters of flashy

parts.note: Jack the Ripper was a murderer in Victorian London

explanation.surface: A nineteenth-century murderer dressed in very gaudy clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: frills, finery and showy ornament in dress.

clue.text: One wrongly copies worker installing shop's interior, you say?

indicators.note: you say means the phrase is pronounced, so the sound gives the answer

parts.note: a tradesman who fits shop counters would be a counter fitter

explanation.surface: A shopfitter gets the job wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: A forger who makes fake banknotes or goods produces illegal copies.

clue.text: Posh colleague supports you and me as a rule

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting pieces sit beneath the first

parts.note: us means you and me
U means upper-class, as in U and non-U
an ally is a friend or colleague

explanation.surface: A smart workmate backs the two of us as a rule.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: normally, generally, in the ordinary course.

clue.text: About fifty falsely accused? There's no way out of this

definitions.text: There's no way out of this

indicators.note: about means around, so the rearranged letters go round fifty
falsely says the following word is put in a false order

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Around fifty people wrongly charged have no means of escape.
explanation.definitionFit: A dead-end street, with no exit other than the way in.

clue.text: Piano work that's heard on Radio One?

definitions.note: chart music played on the station is this genre

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
op, opus, is a musical work

explanation.surface: A piano piece being played on a radio station.
explanation.walkthrough: Radio One is the BBC's national station for chart music.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: chart music is what the BBC's youth station mostly broadcasts.

clue.text: Group of lions were curious, so we're told

indicators.note: so we're told says the word is spoken rather than written

parts.note: pried means were nosy or inquisitive

explanation.surface: Some lions were nosy, according to reports.
explanation.definitionFit: The collective noun for a family group of lions.

clue.text: Agricultural establishment not near motorway

parts.note: far is the opposite of near
M is the abbreviation for motorway, as in M1

explanation.surface: A farm located a long way from the main road.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: land and buildings used for growing crops or rearing animals.

clue.text: Mountain range shown in map book

explanation.surface: A mountain range appears in a book of maps.
explanation.definitionFit: Names both the North African mountains and a bound volume of maps.

clue.text: Swimming pool attendant heads for health centre

indicators.note: heads takes the leading letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: A lifeguard sets off for a health club.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: a resort or club offering treatments and mineral waters.

clue.text: Investigate article discovered in former pit

indicators.note: the article is found inside the pieces that follow

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
a mine is a pit
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Look into an object found in an old coal pit.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: to inspect or look into closely.

clue.text: Request for assistance just after end of April

definitions.meaning: the first of May, the day straight after April ends

explanation.walkthrough: Split into two words, the answer names the 1 May holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: The distress call, and the first day of May.

clue.text: Very little support for drivers west of New York

indicators.note: west of puts this piece to the left in an across answer

parts.note: a golf tee supports the ball for a driver shot

explanation.surface: There is scant help for motorists west of New York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drivers' suggests motorists, but they are golf clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a childish word for something tiny or minute in size.
